title: Repairs and maintenance
description: How to report a repair in a block we manage, and who pays for what under the lease. We arrange the work through contractors from our database.
imageAlt: Plumber repairing the pipes under a sink

intro.heading: How to report a repair
paragraphs: If you live in a building we manage, report repairs to your property manager by phone or email. They deal with repairs to the communal areas: the shared parts of a building or estate, such as halls, stairs, roofs and gardens.

Belgarum Property Management arranges day-to-day repairs and maintenance for every building we manage. We use contractors from our own database and tender work regularly. Specialist work, such as lifts or asbestos, goes to specialist firms.

included.heading: What's included
items: Repairs to the communal areas, and to the other parts of the building that the lease makes the freeholder, resident management company (RMC) or right to manage (RTM) company responsible for
A database of contractors, with work tendered regularly
Specialist firms for lifts, asbestos and fire risk
Regular site inspections, so your property manager can spot problems in the communal areas
Paying for the work from the service charge, as the budget sets out

steps.title: Tell your property manager
steps.text: Contact your property manager by phone or email. Tell them the address, what the problem is, where it is and when it started. Photos help.

steps.title: We check who is responsible
steps.text: The lease decides who repairs what. We check whether the repair is for the building to pay for, or for the owner of a flat.

steps.title: We arrange the work
steps.text: If the repair is the building's responsibility, we instruct a contractor from our database. Larger or specialist jobs may need quotes first.

steps.title: We pay the contractor
steps.text: We pay the contractor's invoice from the building's service charge money. The cost shows in the year-end service charge accounts.

proof: Work is tendered with contractors from our database, so repair costs are compared and your service charge goes further.
We check the lease before any work starts, so the building pays only for the repairs it should.
Your property manager inspects the communal areas regularly, so problems can be spotted before you need to report them.
You report repairs to one dedicated property manager who knows your building.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for repairs inside my flat?
answer: Your lease sets this out. Usually, the leaseholder repairs the inside of their own flat, such as the kitchen, bathroom, internal doors and their own pipes and wiring. Whoever manages the building usually repairs the structure, the roof, the external walls and the communal areas. That can be the freeholder (the owner of the building and the land), a resident management company (RMC) or a right to manage (RTM) company.
If you're not sure, check your lease or contact your property manager.

faqs.question: How do I report a repair?
answer: Contact your property manager by phone on [0800 298 0069](tel:+448002980069) or by email at [management@bpmanagement.org](mailto:management@bpmanagement.org). Our office is open Monday to Thursday, 9am to 5pm, and Friday, 9am to 4.30pm.
If you rent your flat, report repairs inside the flat to your landlord or letting agent.

faqs.question: What should I do in an emergency?
answer: If there is a risk to life, such as a fire, call 999. If you smell gas, call the National Gas Emergency number on [0800 111 999](tel:+44800111999).
For an urgent problem with the building, such as a leak from the roof or a communal pipe, call your property manager on [0800 298 0069](tel:+448002980069) during office hours.

faqs.question: Water is leaking into my flat. What should I do?
answer: If the water is coming from the flat above, contact the people who live there first, as the leak is often inside their flat. If the leak comes from the roof, a communal pipe or a communal area, contact your property manager. Where water is near electrics, turn off the electricity at the consumer unit if it is safe to do so.

faqs.question: Who pays for repairs to the building?
answer: Repairs that the lease makes the building's responsibility are paid from the service charge. The service charge is the money leaseholders pay, under their lease, towards running, repairing and insuring the building. Large, one-off projects are [major works](/services/major-works/), and the law may require leaseholders to be consulted first.
